text:
The week's news for Sam Dickinson is a promotion. Sharks Hockey Digest reported at practice on Nov 13 that "Dickinson Finally Gets PP1 QB Spot", and San Jose Hockey Now spent Saturday asking which of his traits should translate there. His ice time had already jumped: 23.8, 21.8 and 23.5 minutes in his last three games, up from about 18 before.

At 20 he's still learning, and the scoring shows it: 4 points in 20 games. Our comparison helps here. Defensemen picked 6th to 16th since 2005 scored a median 0.25 points a game in their first season of 20-plus games, and he's at 0.20, a little behind but not alarming. At five on five San Jose has had 44.8% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about 2 points better than without him. The tools are obvious: he's one of the fastest skaters in the league (99th percentile top speed). The work in progress is breakouts, where Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had only 30% of his exits keeping possession last season. Running the top power play is the chance to show the 91-point London Knights defenseman is still in there.
headline: Dickinson finally gets the power-play keys
